gen-gf-tapestry-fs-recia: Relaxed neon-tube handwriting from Tapestry meets Recia, whose subtle stroke shading only shows up close. But Recia's generous openings hold at every weight, though it tires over long paragraphs.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads contemporary and friendly, with wide gaps where curves meet stems. Tapestry's hand-drawn heading feels relaxed beside it, and the pairing is happiest with just a few lines of text.
gen-gf-tapestry-outfit: Tapestry writes by hand, its horizontals matching its verticals. It brings relaxed personality to a heading, while Outfit's cable-like sans-serif curves do the quieter work, though not across long paragraphs.
gen-gf-tapestry-sora: Handwritten and easygoing, Tapestry draws each stroke with matching horizontals and verticals. Sora stays crisp and geometric, with no pressure swell at its corners, a good fit for quick glances more than extended reading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-kiwi-maru: Pipe-cleaner strokes and oversized lowercase make Tektur look loud, expressive and unmistakable. Kiwi Maru, a traditional serif with moderate lowercase height beside Tektur's tall one, is the real hook.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Pipe-cleaner strokes give Tektur its odd energy, while Padyakke Expanded One lays out wide, literary letters like knots on a slack rope. Shrink the heading and its quirks fade quickly.
gen-gf-the-girl-next-door-fs-hind: Big, hooked, handwritten letters give The Girl Next Door a graceful, personal swagger. Hind lines up with lowercase nearly matching its capitals and steady strokes, though it wears thin over long paragraphs.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-epunda-slab: Turret Road bends like a paperclip, with round forms like open parentheses. Epunda Slab, a serif with gaping openings and tall rounded lowercase, looks best if you give the heading plenty of size.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-noticia-text: Turret Road draws neon-bright, constant strokes with round, parenthesis-like forms. Noticia Text, a serif whose lowercase fills most of the letter height, gives that boldness a literary, dignified counterpart.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-piazzolla: Turret Road bends neon-tube strokes of constant thickness into bold, commanding letters. And Piazzolla, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals and its e opened like a pried clasp, reads refined and authoritative for long stretches.
